The next MIEM PR to open (after #15) is **the reader for the MVP**, decided with vweeks on 2026-06-15 and announced to K20shores on PR #15. This is the work K20shores deferred ("we can do that next") and the [[project-eccad-reader-debt]] gap.

**Scope (tracked in #6 = MVP species/files, and #16 = real-data reader coverage):**
- **On-mesh reader support** so MIEM can read the real pre-meshed subset `test/data/CAMS-GLOB-ANT_2012_MPAS_bc_subset.nc` (954 KB, already committed). It currently can't — three blockers: vars are `bc_anth_<sector>` + `bc_anth_sum` (not `emi_<species>`); time is `xtime` char strings (not numeric CF time); **no version attribute**.
- **Rename the `convention`** from `"eccad"` to an honest on-mesh name (e.g. `"mpas-flat"` / `"on-mesh"`) — `convention_` default in `include/miem/source_types.hpp` + the `ToLower(convention_)=="eccad"` check in `src/emissions_builder.cpp` + the `ECCADReader` name itself.
- **Likely a SECOND reader** distinct from a future true-ECCAD (lat/lon) reader — K20shores raised this ("we may need to add another reader to actually complete the MVP"). The on-mesh reader and a future ECCAD reader are separate `convention_`/reader selections.
- **Make the README example runnable** on the real BC subset (the Option B endpoint): point at the committed subset, call `Run()`, print per-cell BC flux. BC is an identity species map; the file carries a summed `bc_anth_sum`.
- **Surgical doc edits** in `docs/config-architecture.md`: flip `convention: eccad` → the new on-mesh name in §6's YAML example and §7's convention-check row, and supersede the 2026-06-15 Update block's "currently labelled `eccad`" phrasing. (This is why #15 only added the governing Update block, not the rename — see #15.)

**Constraints / facts:**
- The BC subset is **black-carbon-only**, so it does NOT satisfy #6's NO2/NO/O3 acceptance criterion — those stay synthetic in `test/integration/test_nox_pipeline.cpp` (or need a separate NOx/O3 inventory).
- MVP convention is on-mesh; **ECCAD-proper (lat/lon) + remapping is a LATER phase** / a separate model-agnostic "build-once emissions store" tool (concept doc at `~/NCAR/acom/CheMPAS/emissions-store-concept/`). Do NOT pull remapping into MIEM's runtime; `Regridding` stays a v1 `None`-only guard.
- K20shores did NOT pick README Option A (synthetic-in-PR) vs B (real-data-via-reader); he leaned toward the reader path → **we chose B / the reader**. A is set aside.

**Why:** vweeks scoped this over a long 2026-06-15 design session; it's the agreed next milestone and the resolution of the long-standing reader debt. **How to apply:** when resuming MIEM PR work, open this as a new PR off `main` (NOT stacked on #15). Respect [[project_off_limits]]. See [[project-eccad-reader-debt]] for the reader specifics and [[feedback-pre-review-sweep]] before assigning K20shores.

=== ISSUE 6 (MVP) ===
{"body":"To prove we are ready, we will set up an integration test that replicates — in a box (or column, or gridded) model — what needs to be done in MPAS.

## Species the MVP must read and produce
- **NO2, NO, O3** — from a NOx + O3 inventory: NOx → NO (0.9) / NO2 (0.1) speciation split, O3 passthrough (identity).
- **Black carbon (BC)** — from the regridded CAMS anthropogenic sectors (`bc_anth_<sector>` → BC), single-species identity map.

## Files the MVP must read
- **Synthetic on-mesh fixture** (`emi_NOx`, `emi_O3`): drives the exact-value NO/NO2/O3 assertions in `test/integration/test_nox_pipeline.cpp`. Shape `(Time, nCells)`, numeric CF-time, version attribute — the contract the current reader expects.
- **Real on-mesh subset** `test/data/CAMS-GLOB-ANT_2012_MPAS_bc_subset.nc`: every 40th cell of the UPTEMPO-remapped x1.163842 mesh, all 12 BC sectors + `bc_anth_sum`, 12 months. Layout: `bc_anth_<sector>(Time, nCells)`, `xtime` char strings, **no version attribute**.

## Reader requirement
The current `ECCADReader` consumes the synthetic `emi_*` / numeric-CF-time / version-attr contract. Reading the **real** BC subset requires on-mesh-layout support (`bc_anth_*`, `xtime`, no version attr) — tracked in #16 — and likely a **second reader** (an on-mesh / MPAS-flat reader, distinct from the ECCAD reader).

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] An integration test that gets emissions for **NO2, NO, and O3** from a synthetic on-mesh inventory — `test/integration/test_nox_pipeline.cpp`.
- [ ] An integration test (or runnable README example) that reads the **real** on-mesh BC subset and produces per-cell BC surface flux — depends on the reader work in #16.

## Scope note
The MVP consumes data **already on the model mesh** (remapped offline by UPTEMPO); it does not remap. ECCAD-native (lat/lon) format enforcement is a later, remapping-phase concern — the MVP's input convention is "on-mesh." Remapping itself is out of MIEM's runtime scope (a separate preprocessing step / tool).

38	///        @c EmissionsBuilder.
39	///
40	/// MIEM mirrors MICM: there is no aggregate "config" object. A host (or
41	/// musica's translator) hands the runtime a collection of domain objects,
42	/// and @c Source is that object -- the emissions analog of a single
43	/// @c micm::Process. Add one per inventory to an @c EmissionsBuilder.
44	///
45	/// A @c Source is a plain value type: it holds no open files or runtime
46	/// state. The builder turns each @c Source into a runtime @c EmissionSource
47	/// (via @c SourceFactory) when @c EmissionsBuilder::Build() is called. All
48	/// field names carry a trailing underscore.
49	///
50	/// Category and hierarchy follow the HEMCO pattern:
51	/// - Sources in different categories are summed.
52	/// - Within a category, the highest-hierarchy source wins per cell.
53	///
54	/// Duplicate (category, hierarchy) pairs are rejected at @c Build() time.
55	struct Source
56	{
57	  std::string name_;                              ///< Diagnostic name for the source.
58	  SourceMode  mode_ = SourceMode::Offline;        ///< Offline files vs online computation.
59	  SourceType  type_ = SourceType::Anthropogenic;  ///< Inventory sector.
60	
61	  /// File pattern with optional @c {YYYY}{MM}{DD}{HH} tokens. Already
62	  /// resolved by musica's translator: MIEM receives a concrete path.
63	  std::string file_pattern_;
64	
65	  /// Inventory convention: the on-disk NetCDF layout MIEM assumes when it
66	  /// reads this source's files. v1 accepts only "eccad" (case-insensitive);
67	  /// anything else is @c UnknownConvention at build time.
68	  ///
69	  /// The "eccad" convention follows the file layout published by ECCAD
70	  /// (Emissions of atmospheric Compounds and Compilation of Ancillary Data,
71	  /// https://eccad.aeris-data.fr/) -- the AERIS-hosted repository MIEM's
72	  /// reference inventories (e.g. CAMS-GLOB-ANT) are distributed through.
73	  /// See the "Inventory conventions" page of the user guide for the
74	  /// variable/dimension/units expectations this implies, and for how
75	  /// non-conforming files are adapted via a dataset descriptor.
76	  std::string convention_ = "eccad";
77	
78	  /// Inventory-to-mechanism species map: rewrites this source's emission
79	  /// flux from the inventory's species names onto the chemical mechanism's
80	  /// species (the names MICM solves for), redistributing mass per the
81	  /// configured per-mapping scaling factors. It maps emission *flux*, not
82	  /// concentration, and only renames/splits species -- it does not itself
83	  /// move data between MIEM and MICM. musica builds it by translating the
84	  /// parsed configuration's named @c species_map entry. See
85	  /// @ref SpeciesMap::Apply for the transform.
86	  SpeciesMap species_map_;
87	
88	  /// @brief Interpolation between successive input time slices.
89	  TemporalInterpolation temporal_interpolation_ = TemporalInterpolation::Linear;
90	
91	  /// @brief Vertical placement of the emitted mass.
92	  VerticalInjection vertical_injection_ = VerticalInjection::Surface;
93	
94	  int  category_       = 0;    ///< HEMCO category index.
95	  int  hierarchy_      = 1;    ///< HEMCO hierarchy level.
96	  Real scaling_factor_ = 1.0;  ///< Multiplicative flux scaling.
97	
98	  std::string sector_;  ///< Optional diagnostic label.
99	};

# Test data

Small, real emission fixtures committed for MIEM's tests. Kept to a few MB so
they live in plain git (no LFS).

## `CAMS-GLOB-ANT_2012_MPAS_bc_subset.nc` (932 KB)

A heavily-reduced but **real** slice of the CAMS-GLOB-ANT v6.2 black-carbon
emissions for 2012, in the MPAS-regridded ("UPTEMPO output") layout that MIEM's
`"eccad"`-convention reader consumes — i.e. flux laid out flat on the MPAS mesh
(`Time`, `nCells`), not the raw ECCAD lat/lon grid.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Source | `CAMS-GLOB-ANT_2012_MPAS.x1.163842.grid.bc_c20260508.nc` (94 MB, Forrest Lacey & Rajesh Kumar) |
| Reduction | every 40th cell of the `x1.163842` mesh → **4097 of 163842 cells** |
| Retained | all 12 anthropogenic BC sectors (`bc_anth_awb…bc_anth_sum`), all 12 months, `xtime` |
| Values | unmodified — real `kg m-2 s-1` fluxes (provenance stamped in the `subset_*` global attributes) |

The cells are sampled by a global stride rather than a contiguous block: an MPAS
mesh is not spatially ordered, so striding keeps a worldwide land/ocean mix
(≈39k of the 49k cell-months carry nonzero emissions) instead of one local
patch.

### Why it's here before there's a reader

This file is committed by the `Source`-schema PR, which has no file reader yet —
it answers a reviewer request to have real data on hand and pre-positions the
fixture so the ECCAD-reader PR can wire a read test against it without
re-sourcing data.

### Regenerating

```sh
python3 -m pip install netCDF4 numpy
python3 tools/subset_eccad.py <full_MPAS_grid_file>.nc \
    test/data/CAMS-GLOB-ANT_2012_MPAS_bc_subset.nc 40
```

I now have a complete picture of the architecture. Let me share what I found, then settle a couple of consequential design decisions before writing code.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
The reader pipeline is cleanly layered and polymorphic: `EmissionSource` (abstract) → `OfflineEmissionSource` (PIMPL-wrapping a private `ECCADReader`) → `SourceFactory::Create()` dispatches on `convention_`. The `ECCADReader` is the only NetCDF-aware code, deliberately kept out of public headers. This is exactly the seam K20shores designed for "add another reader" — a new reader is a new factory branch, not a rewrite.

The naming debt is real and now concrete: the so-called `ECCADReader` consumes `emi_<species>` / numeric CF `time` / `n_cells` / a required `eccad_version` attribute — but the **real** committed fixture has `bc_anth_<sector>` / `xtime` char strings / `Time`+`nCells` / **no** version attribute. So the current reader cannot open the real MVP data at all — four independent mismatches.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

Here's the gap, confirmed against live code and the real `ncdump`:

| Aspect | Existing `ECCADReader` expects | Real CAMS fixture has |
|---|---|---|
| Flux vars | `emi_<species>` | `bc_anth_<sector>` (+ `bc_anth_sum`) |
| Time | numeric `time` var + CF `units` | `xtime` char strings (`Time,StrLen`) |
| Dims | `time` / `n_cells` | `Time` / `nCells` |
| Format gate | requires `eccad_version` attr | none (only `authors`/`time_created`) |

Two decisions here are reviewer-facing and hard to reverse (K20shores cares a lot about naming/ecosystem parity, and he invested in the ECCAD docs in PR #12). Let me lock these before writing code.

38	```bash
39	git clone https://github.com/NCAR/miem.git
40	cd miem
41	docker build -t miem -f docker/Dockerfile .
42	docker run -it miem bash
43	```
44	
45	Inside the container, you can run the MIEM tests from the `/build/` folder:
46	
47	```bash
48	cd /build/
49	make test
50	```
51	
52	## Using the MIEM API
53	
54	The following example describes a single anthropogenic emissions source and assembles it into an `Emissions` module with `EmissionsBuilder`.  Following micm, MIEM has no aggregate configuration object: you hand the builder `Source` domain objects and it validates and builds the module in `Build()`.
55	
56	Species mapping and inventory translation are handled upstream by `MechanismConfiguration` and `musica::Translate()`.  By the time a `Source` is constructed here, every named reference has been resolved into a flat struct that MIEM owns.  MIEM does not parse YAML at any level.
57	
58	To run this example save the following code in a file named `miem_example.cpp`:
59	
60	```cpp
61	#include <miem/miem.hpp>
62	
63	#include <iostream>
64	
65	using namespace miem;
66	
67	int main()
68	{
69	  Source cams_anthro;
70	  cams_anthro.name_                   = "CAMS anthropogenic";
71	  cams_anthro.mode_                   = SourceMode::Offline;
72	  cams_anthro.type_                   = SourceType::Anthropogenic;
73	  cams_anthro.file_pattern_           = "/path/to/CAMS-GLOB-ANT_{YYYY}-{MM}.nc";
74	  cams_anthro.convention_             = "eccad";
75	  cams_anthro.temporal_interpolation_ = TemporalInterpolation::Linear;
76	  cams_anthro.vertical_injection_     = VerticalInjection::Surface;
77	  cams_anthro.category_               = 0;
78	  cams_anthro.hierarchy_              = 1;
79	  cams_anthro.scaling_factor_         = 1.0;
80	  cams_anthro.sector_                 = "anthropogenic";
81	
82	  // Programmatic species map: NOx -> NO (0.9), NOx -> NO2 (0.1).
83	  cams_anthro.species_map_.AddMapping("NOx", "NO",  0.9);
84	  cams_anthro.species_map_.AddMapping("NOx", "NO2", 0.1);
85	
86	  try
87	  {
88	    // EmissionsBuilder assembles Source descriptions into a runtime
89	    // module, mirroring micm's CpuSolverBuilder.  Build() validates the
90	    // configuration and throws miem::MiemException if any invariant fails.
91	    Emissions emissions = EmissionsBuilder()
92	                              .SetGridDimensions(/*n_cells=*/163842,
93	                                                 /*n_vert_levels=*/60)
94	                              .AddSource(cams_anthro)
95	                              .Build();
96	
97	    std::cout << "emissions advertises " << emissions.NumSpecies()
98	              << " mechanism species\n";
99	
100	    // emissions.Run(sim_time_sec, dt_sec) returns an EmissionsState and
101	    // throws miem::MiemException on failure; the overload taking
102	    // air_density/layer_thickness arrays additionally populates
103	    // state.tendency_ via FluxConverter.
104	  }
105	  catch (const miem::MiemException& e)
106	  {
107	    std::cerr << "configuration invalid [" << e.Category() << '/' << e.Code()
108	              << "]: " << e.what() << "\n";
109	    return 1;
110	  }
111	
112	  return 0;
113	}
114	```
115

117	
118	```cmake
119	find_package(miem CONFIG REQUIRED)
120	target_link_libraries(my_app PRIVATE musica::miem)
121	```

1	#####################
2	Inventory Conventions
3	#####################
4	
5	Every emission ``miem::Source`` names an *inventory convention* (its
6	``convention_`` field) that tells MIEM how the source's NetCDF files are laid
7	out on disk. The convention is a contract about variable names, dimensions,
8	and units -- not about the science of the inventory itself. In v1 MIEM
9	supports a single convention, ``"eccad"``; any other value is rejected as
10	``UnknownConvention`` when the emissions builder builds the runtime.
11	
12	Why ECCAD
13	=========
14	
15	MIEM's reference emission inventories are distributed through ECCAD
16	:cite:`ECCAD` (Emissions of atmospheric Compounds and Compilation of Ancillary
17	Data, https://eccad.aeris-data.fr/), the atmospheric-emissions data repository
18	hosted by `AERIS <https://www.aeris-data.fr/>`_. Datasets such as
19	CAMS-GLOB-ANT (anthropogenic) and GFAS (biomass burning) are published there in
20	a consistent NetCDF layout, and that layout is what MIEM's ``"eccad"``
21	convention encodes. Standardizing on the ECCAD layout means a host model can
22	point MIEM at a freshly downloaded inventory without writing a bespoke reader
23	for each product.
24	
25	This is a *file-format* dependency, not a network or runtime dependency: MIEM
26	never contacts ECCAD. A user (or musica's translator) downloads the files
27	ahead of time and hands MIEM a concrete, already-resolved path through
28	``Source::file_pattern_``.
29	
30	What the convention assumes
31	===========================
32	
33	The ``"eccad"`` convention expects each file to provide, per emitted species:
34	
35	- a flux variable keyed by the inventory's species name,
36	- a mass-flux unit of ``kg m-2 s-1`` (the canonical ECCAD emission unit),
37	- a ``time`` dimension MIEM interpolates across successive slices, and
38	- a horizontal cell dimension already on the target grid (v1 does no
39	  regridding).
40	
41	The inventory's species names rarely match the chemical mechanism's names.
42	That gap is closed *after* the file is read, by the source's ``SpeciesMap``,
43	which rewrites inventory-named emission flux onto the mechanism species MICM
44	solves for.
45	
46	Non-conforming files
47	====================
48	
49	Inventories that do not follow the ECCAD layout (legacy CEDS files, custom
50	research products) are not read with a second hard-coded convention. Instead,
51	upstream tooling attaches a *dataset descriptor* that names the variable
52	prefix, units, and dimension names so the file can be adapted to the canonical
53	layout. The descriptor mechanism is defined in the configuration schema and
54	resolved by musica before MIEM runs; the load-time versus runtime split is
55	described in the configuration architecture note (``docs/config-architecture.md``
56	in the repository). For v1, only ``"eccad"`` is accepted directly.

#####################
Inventory Conventions
#####################

Every emission ``miem::Source`` names an *inventory convention* (its
``convention_`` field) that tells MIEM how the source's NetCDF files are laid
out on disk. The convention is a contract about variable names, dimensions,
and units -- not about the science of the inventory itself. In v1 MIEM
supports a single convention, ``"eccad"``; any other value is rejected as
``UnknownConvention`` when the emissions builder builds the runtime.

Why ECCAD
=========

MIEM's reference emission inventories are distributed through ECCAD
:cite:`ECCAD` (Emissions of atmospheric Compounds and Compilation of Ancillary
Data, https://eccad.aeris-data.fr/), the atmospheric-emissions data repository
hosted by `AERIS <https://www.aeris-data.fr/>`_. Datasets such as
CAMS-GLOB-ANT (anthropogenic) and GFAS (biomass burning) are published there in
a consistent NetCDF layout, and that layout is what MIEM's ``"eccad"``
convention encodes. Standardizing on the ECCAD layout means a host model can
point MIEM at a freshly downloaded inventory without writing a bespoke reader
for each product.

This is a *file-format* dependency, not a network or runtime dependency: MIEM
never contacts ECCAD. A user (or musica's translator) downloads the files
ahead of time and hands MIEM a concrete, already-resolved path through
``Source::file_pattern_``.

What the convention assumes
===========================

The ``"eccad"`` convention expects each file to provide, per emitted species:

- a flux variable keyed by the inventory's species name,
- a mass-flux unit of ``kg m-2 s-1`` (the canonical ECCAD emission unit),
- a ``time`` dimension MIEM interpolates across successive slices, and
- a horizontal cell dimension already on the target grid (v1 does no
  regridding).

The inventory's species names rarely match the chemical mechanism's names.
That gap is closed *after* the file is read, by the source's ``SpeciesMap``,
which rewrites inventory-named emission flux onto the mechanism species MICM
solves for.

Non-conforming files
====================

Inventories that do not follow the ECCAD layout (legacy CEDS files, custom
research products) are not read with a second hard-coded convention. Instead,
upstream tooling attaches a *dataset descriptor* that names the variable
prefix, units, and dimension names so the file can be adapted to the canonical
layout. The descriptor mechanism is defined in the configuration schema and
resolved by musica before MIEM runs; the load-time versus runtime split is
described in the configuration architecture note (``docs/config-architecture.md``
in the repository). For v1, only ``"eccad"`` is accepted directly.

  find_program(MEMORYCHECK_COMMAND "valgrind")

function(create_standard_test)
  set(prefix TEST)
  set(singleValues NAME WORKING_DIRECTORY)
  set(multiValues SOURCES LIBRARIES)
  include(CMakeParseArguments)
  cmake_parse_arguments(${prefix} " " "${singleValues}" "${multiValues}" ${ARGN})

#####################
Inventory Conventions
#####################

Every emission ``miem::Source`` names an *inventory convention* (its
``convention_`` field) that tells MIEM how the source's NetCDF files are laid
out on disk. The convention is a contract about variable names, dimensions,
and units -- not about the science of the inventory itself. In v1 MIEM
supports a single convention, ``"eccad"``; any other value is rejected as
``UnknownConvention`` when the emissions builder builds the runtime.

Why ECCAD
=========

MIEM's reference emission inventories are distributed through ECCAD
:cite:`ECCAD` (Emissions of atmospheric Compounds and Compilation of Ancillary
Data, https://eccad.aeris-data.fr/), the atmospheric-emissions data repository
hosted by `AERIS <https://www.aeris-data.fr/>`_. Datasets such as
CAMS-GLOB-ANT (anthropogenic) and GFAS (biomass burning) are published there in
a consistent NetCDF layout, and that layout is what MIEM's ``"eccad"``
convention encodes. Standardizing on the ECCAD layout means a host model can
point MIEM at a freshly downloaded inventory without writing a bespoke reader
for each product.

This is a *file-format* dependency, not a network or runtime dependency: MIEM
never contacts ECCAD. A user (or musica's translator) downloads the files
ahead of time and hands MIEM a concrete, already-resolved path through
``Source::file_pattern_``.

What the convention assumes
===========================

The ``"eccad"`` convention expects each file to provide, per emitted species:

- a flux variable keyed by the inventory's species name,
- a mass-flux unit of ``kg m-2 s-1`` (the canonical ECCAD emission unit),
- a ``time`` dimension MIEM interpolates across successive slices, and
- a horizontal cell dimension already on the target grid (v1 does no
  regridding).

The inventory's species names rarely match the chemical mechanism's names.
That gap is closed *after* the file is read, by the source's ``SpeciesMap``,
which rewrites inventory-named emission flux onto the mechanism species MICM
solves for.

Non-conforming files
====================

Inventories that do not follow the ECCAD layout (legacy CEDS files, custom
research products) are not read with a second hard-coded convention. Instead,
upstream tooling attaches a *dataset descriptor* that names the variable
prefix, units, and dimension names so the file can be adapted to the canonical
layout. The descriptor mechanism is defined in the configuration schema and
resolved by musica before MIEM runs; the load-time versus runtime split is
described in the configuration architecture note (``docs/config-architecture.md``
in the repository). For v1, only ``"eccad"`` is accepted directly.

The UPTEMPO on-mesh convention
==============================

The ``"uptempo"`` convention reads inventories that have already been
remapped onto the model's MPAS mesh by the UPTEMPO preprocessor -- the form
MIEM consumes for the v1 MVP. It differs from ``"eccad"`` in three ways:

- flux fields are whatever ``(Time, nCells)`` variables the file carries,
  keyed by their own variable names (for example ``bc_anth_ene`` or the
  precomputed ``bc_anth_sum``). There is no ``emi_`` prefix, and the reader
  makes no assumption about the species or sector naming scheme, so it works
  for any UPTEMPO-remapped inventory.
- the time axis is the MPAS ``xtime`` character variable, holding
  ``YYYY-MM-DD_HH:MM:SS`` strings, rather than a numeric ``time`` variable
  with CF ``units``.
- the mesh is identified by the ``Time`` / ``nCells`` dimensions; there is
  no version global attribute to gate on.

As with ``"eccad"``, the source's ``SpeciesMap`` closes the gap between the
file's variable names and the mechanism species -- for example mapping
``bc_anth_sum`` onto a mechanism's black-carbon species. A reduced, real
fixture in this layout ships at
``test/data/CAMS-GLOB-ANT_2012_MPAS_bc_subset.nc``, and the ``bc_pipeline``
integration test reads it end to end.

#####################
Inventory Conventions
#####################

Every emission ``miem::Source`` names an *inventory convention* (its
``convention_`` field) that tells MIEM how the source's NetCDF files are laid
out on disk. The convention is a contract about variable names, dimensions,
and units -- not about the science of the inventory itself. In v1 MIEM
supports two conventions, ``"eccad"`` and ``"uptempo"`` (case-insensitive);
any other value is rejected as ``UnknownConvention`` when the emissions
builder builds the runtime.

Why ECCAD
=========

MIEM's reference emission inventories are distributed through ECCAD
:cite:`ECCAD` (Emissions of atmospheric Compounds and Compilation of Ancillary
Data, https://eccad.aeris-data.fr/), the atmospheric-emissions data repository
hosted by `AERIS <https://www.aeris-data.fr/>`_. Datasets such as
CAMS-GLOB-ANT (anthropogenic) and GFAS (biomass burning) are published there in
a consistent NetCDF layout, and that layout is what MIEM's ``"eccad"``
convention encodes. Standardizing on the ECCAD layout means a host model can
point MIEM at a freshly downloaded inventory without writing a bespoke reader
for each product.

This is a *file-format* dependency, not a network or runtime dependency: MIEM
never contacts ECCAD. A user (or musica's translator) downloads the files
ahead of time and hands MIEM a concrete, already-resolved path through
``Source::file_pattern_``.

What the convention assumes
===========================

The ``"eccad"`` convention expects each file to provide, per emitted species:

- a flux variable keyed by the inventory's species name,
- a mass-flux unit of ``kg m-2 s-1`` (the canonical ECCAD emission unit),
- a ``time`` dimension MIEM interpolates across successive slices, and
- a horizontal cell dimension already on the target grid (v1 does no
  regridding).

The inventory's species names rarely match the chemical mechanism's names.
That gap is closed *after* the file is read, by the source's ``SpeciesMap``,
which rewrites inventory-named emission flux onto the mechanism species MICM
solves for.

The UPTEMPO on-mesh convention
==============================

The ``"uptempo"`` convention reads inventories that have already been
remapped onto the model's MPAS mesh by the UPTEMPO preprocessor -- the form
MIEM consumes for the v1 MVP. It differs from ``"eccad"`` in three ways:

- flux fields are whatever ``(Time, nCells)`` variables the file carries,
  keyed by their own variable names (for example ``bc_anth_ene`` or the
  precomputed ``bc_anth_sum``). There is no ``emi_`` prefix, and the reader
  makes no assumption about the species or sector naming scheme, so it works
  for any UPTEMPO-remapped inventory.
- the time axis is the MPAS ``xtime`` character variable, holding
  ``YYYY-MM-DD_HH:MM:SS`` strings, rather than a numeric ``time`` variable
  with CF ``units``.
- the mesh is identified by the ``Time`` / ``nCells`` dimensions; there is
  no version global attribute to gate on.

As with ``"eccad"``, the source's ``SpeciesMap`` closes the gap between the
file's variable names and the mechanism species -- for example mapping
``bc_anth_sum`` onto a mechanism's black-carbon species. A reduced, real
fixture in this layout ships at
``test/data/CAMS-GLOB-ANT_2012_MPAS_bc_subset.nc``, and the ``bc_pipeline``
integration test reads it end to end.

Non-conforming files
====================

Inventories that do not follow the ECCAD layout (legacy CEDS files, custom
research products) are not read with a second hard-coded convention. Instead,
upstream tooling attaches a *dataset descriptor* that names the variable
prefix, units, and dimension names so the file can be adapted to the canonical
layout. The descriptor mechanism is defined in the configuration schema and
resolved by musica before MIEM runs; the load-time versus runtime split is
described in the configuration architecture note (``docs/config-architecture.md``
in the repository). For v1, only ``"eccad"`` is accepted directly.

# Test data

Small, real emission fixtures committed for MIEM's tests. Kept to a few MB so
they live in plain git (no LFS).

## `CAMS-GLOB-ANT_2012_MPAS_bc_subset.nc` (932 KB)

A heavily-reduced but **real** slice of the CAMS-GLOB-ANT v6.2 black-carbon
emissions for 2012, in the MPAS-regridded ("UPTEMPO output") layout that MIEM's
`"eccad"`-convention reader consumes — i.e. flux laid out flat on the MPAS mesh
(`Time`, `nCells`), not the raw ECCAD lat/lon grid.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Source | `CAMS-GLOB-ANT_2012_MPAS.x1.163842.grid.bc_c20260508.nc` (94 MB, Forrest Lacey & Rajesh Kumar) |
| Reduction | every 40th cell of the `x1.163842` mesh → **4097 of 163842 cells** |
| Retained | all 12 anthropogenic BC sectors (`bc_anth_awb…bc_anth_sum`), all 12 months, `xtime` |
| Values | unmodified — real `kg m-2 s-1` fluxes (provenance stamped in the `subset_*` global attributes) |

The cells are sampled by a global stride rather than a contiguous block: an MPAS
mesh is not spatially ordered, so striding keeps a worldwide land/ocean mix
(≈39k of the 49k cell-months carry nonzero emissions) instead of one local
patch.

### Why it's here before there's a reader

This file is committed by the `Source`-schema PR, which has no file reader yet —
it answers a reviewer request to have real data on hand and pre-positions the
fixture so the ECCAD-reader PR can wire a read test against it without
re-sourcing data.

### Regenerating

```sh
python3 -m pip install netCDF4 numpy
python3 tools/subset_eccad.py <full_MPAS_grid_file>.nc \
    test/data/CAMS-GLOB-ANT_2012_MPAS_bc_subset.nc 40
```

Committed locally on `feature/uptempo-reader` (off `main`, not stacked on #15). Here's what landed.

## Summary — the UPTEMPO on-mesh reader (the MVP reader)

**The gap it closes:** MIEM literally could not open the real committed fixture. The ECCAD reader requires `emi_<species>` vars, numeric CF `time`, an `n_cells` dim, and a version attribute — the real CAMS-on-MPAS file has `bc_anth_*` vars, `xtime` strings, `Time`/`nCells` dims, and no version attribute.

**What I built (per your two decisions — keep `eccad` as-is, new `"uptempo"` convention, *not* hardcoded to `bc_anth`):**

- **`UptempoReader`** (`src/uptempo_reader.cpp`) — discovers *any* `(Time, nCells)` flux field by its own variable name (works for any UPTEMPO-remapped inventory, not just black carbon), decodes MPAS `xtime` (`YYYY-MM-DD_HH:MM:SS`), needs no version attribute, and zeroes NaN-masked ocean cells.
- **Polymorphic readers** — extracted an internal `EmissionFileReader` interface; `OfflineEmissionSource` now holds the interface and a **`reader_factory`** owns the *single* `convention → reader` mapping. This collapsed the convention list that previously lived in **three** places (builder, source factory, wiring) down to one.
- **`netcdf_io.hpp`** — lifted the shared NetCDF boilerplate (~60 lines) so both readers use it. The ECCAD reader is a pure de-dup, **no behavior change** (`"eccad"` untouched, its test still green).
- **Tests** — `uptempo_reader` unit test (real fixture + synthetic xtime/NaN/generic-discovery/rejection cases) and a **`bc_pipeline`** integration test running the full pipeline (`bc_anth_sum → BC`) against the real subset to per-cell flux. **This is the real-data MVP** — closes #16 and issue #6's 2nd acceptance criterion.
- **Docs** — user-guide conventions page, runnable README example, and `test/data/README.md`. I deliberately **left `docs/config-architecture.md` alone** (it's what the held #15 rewrites — editing it here would collide).

**Verification:** clean build, **0 compiler warnings, 0 clang-tidy warnings**, **13/13 tests pass** (incl. the 2 new).

## What & why

MIEM could not read the real fixture committed in #12 (`test/data/CAMS-GLOB-ANT_2012_MPAS_bc_subset.nc`). The existing ECCAD reader expects an idealized contract — `emi_<species>` variables, a numeric CF `time` axis, an `n_cells` dimension, and a version global attribute — while the real CAMS data, already remapped onto the MPAS mesh by UPTEMPO, has `bc_anth_<sector>` variables, an `xtime` character time axis, `Time`/`nCells` dimensions, and no version attribute. This PR makes MIEM read that real data end to end — the MVP reader.

## Approach

A **second reader**, selected by a new `"uptempo"` `Source` convention, rather than bending the ECCAD reader (which backs the exact-value NOx/O3 integration test). The synthetic test data already matches the `"eccad"` contract, so that reader and convention are **left unchanged**.

- **`UptempoReader`** reads the on-mesh layout directly:
  - discovers **any** `(Time, nCells)` flux field by its own variable name — no `emi_` prefix and no hard-coded species/sector scheme, so it works for any UPTEMPO-remapped inventory, not just black carbon;
  - decodes the MPAS `xtime` character axis (`YYYY-MM-DD_HH:MM:SS`);
  - identifies the mesh by the `Time`/`nCells` dimensions, with no version attribute required;
  - zeroes NaN-masked (e.g. ocean) cells.
- **Readers are now polymorphic** behind an internal `EmissionFileReader` interface. `OfflineEmissionSource` holds the interface, and a new `reader_factory` owns the single `convention → reader` mapping that both `EmissionsBuilder::Validate()` and the source constructor defer to (previously the convention list lived in three places).
- Shared NetCDF boilerplate moves to `internal/netcdf_io.hpp`; this is a **pure de-dup of the ECCAD reader with no behavior change**.

## Tests

- `uptempo_reader` unit test — exercises the **real** fixture (open without a version attribute, variable discovery, `xtime` decoding, NaN handling) plus deterministic synthetic cases (xtime → epoch seconds, generic non-`bc_anth` variable discovery, NaN-zeroing, missing-time rejection, and rejection of an ECCAD-layout file).
- `bc_pipeline` integration test — runs the full builder → source → reader → species-map → `Run()` pipeline against the real subset, mapping `bc_anth_sum → BC`, asserting finite, non-negative, non-trivial per-cell surface flux. This is the runnable counterpart of the new README example.

Local: clean build, **0 compiler warnings, 0 clang-tidy warnings, 13/13 tests pass**.

## Scope notes

- Closes #16 (real-data integration coverage once the reader supports the CAMS MPAS sector layout). Delivers issue #6's second acceptance criterion (read the real on-mesh BC subset → per-cell BC flux); the NOx/O3 exact-value path stays synthetic as designed.
- The black-carbon subset is BC-only, so it does not cover #6's NO2/NO/O3 criterion — those remain on the synthetic `emi_*` path.
- `docs/config-architecture.md` is intentionally **not** touched here (it is the subject of the in-flight docs PR #15); the `convention` wording there is left to that PR.
- ECCAD-native (lat/lon) reading and remapping remain out of scope (a later phase / separate tool).

# -- Path setup --------------------------------------------------------------

import os
import sys
import datetime
import re
import subprocess
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.abspath('.'))

DOCS_SOURCE_DIR = os.path.abspath(os.path.dirname(__file__))
REPO_ROOT_DIR = os.path.abspath(os.path.join(DOCS_SOURCE_DIR, '..', '..'))
BUILD_DIR = os.path.join(REPO_ROOT_DIR, 'build')
DOXYGEN_XML_DIR = os.path.join(BUILD_DIR, 'docs', 'doxygen', 'xml')


def _run_command(command, cwd=None):
    try:
        subprocess.run(command, cwd=cwd, check=True)
    except (OSError, subprocess.CalledProcessError) as exc:
        sys.stderr.write(f"Command failed: {command}\n{exc}\n")
        raise


def _ensure_doxygen_xml():
    # On Read the Docs the Doxygen XML is generated by the CMake build in the
    # .readthedocs.yaml pre_build step; this hook makes conf.py self-sufficient
    # for a bare ``sphinx-build`` as well.
    read_the_docs_build = os.environ.get('READTHEDOCS', None) == 'True'
    if not read_the_docs_build:
        return

    cache_file = os.path.join(BUILD_DIR, 'CMakeCache.txt')
    if not os.path.exists(cache_file):
        _run_command([
            'cmake',
            '-S', REPO_ROOT_DIR,
            '-B', BUILD_DIR,
            '-D', 'MIEM_BUILD_DOCS=ON',
            '-D', 'MIEM_ENABLE_TESTS=OFF',
        ])

    _run_command([
        'cmake',
        '--build', BUILD_DIR,
        '--target', 'Doxygen',
    ])

# -- Project information -----------------------------------------------------

project = 'MIEM'
copyright = f'2024-{datetime.datetime.now().year}, NSF-NCAR/ACOM'
author = 'NSF-NCAR/ACOM'

regex = r'project\(\w+\s+VERSION\s+(\d+\.\d+\.\d+)'
version = '0.0.0'
# read the version from the cmake files
with open(os.path.join(REPO_ROOT_DIR, 'CMakeLists.txt'), 'r') as f:
    for line in f:
        match = re.match(regex, line)
        if match:
            version = match.group(1)
release = f'{version}'

# ones.

    'breathe',

    'sphinxcontrib.bibtex',
    'sphinx.ext.intersphinx',
]

bibtex_bibfiles = ['references.bib']
suppress_warnings = ["bibtex.missing_field"]

breathe_default_project = "miem"
breathe_projects = {
    "miem": DOXYGEN_XML_DIR
}

# Add any paths that contain templates here, relative to this directory.

# List of patterns, relative to source directory, that match files and

    'micm': ('https://ncar.github.io/micm/', None),

}

# -- Options for HTML output -------------------------------------------------

# The theme to use for HTML and HTML Help pages.
html_theme = 'pydata_sphinx_theme'

html_theme_options = {
    "external_links": [],
    "github_url": "https://github.com/NCAR/miem",
    "navbar_end": ["navbar-icon-links"],
    "pygment_light_style": "tango",

}

html_css_files = [
    'custom.css'
]

# Add any paths that contain custom static files (such as style sheets) here,
# relative to this directory.
html_static_path = ['_static']


def setup(app):
    app.connect("builder-inited", lambda _app: _ensure_doxygen_xml())

content.text:
This is **#18 — "feat: UPTEMPO on-mesh reader for real CAMS emissions"** (off `main`, closes #16 and delivers issue #6's second acceptance criterion). Here's what's in it:

## The core feature
**A second NetCDF reader (`UptempoReader`)** so MIEM can read the *real* committed fixture (`test/data/CAMS-GLOB-ANT_2012_MPAS_bc_subset.nc`), which the existing ECCAD reader couldn't open. Selected by a new `Source.convention_ = "uptempo"`. It:
- discovers flux fields **generically** — any `(Time, nCells)` variable by its own name, so it's not tied to `bc_anth_*` or any one inventory's naming;
- decodes the MPAS `xtime` character time axis (`YYYY-MM-DD_HH:MM:SS`);
- needs **no version attribute** (identifies the layout by the `Time`/`nCells` dims);
- zeroes NaN-masked (e.g. ocean) cells.

## Supporting architecture
- **Polymorphic readers**: extracted an internal `EmissionFileReader` interface + a `reader_factory` that owns the single `convention → reader` mapping (collapsed a convention check that was duplicated in 3 places down to 1). The **ECCAD reader and `"eccad"` convention are unchanged** — it just adopts the interface.
- **`internal/netcdf_io.hpp`**: shared NetCDF helper boilerplate, de-duplicated between the two readers (no behavior change to ECCAD).

## Tests
- `test_uptempo_reader` (unit) — real fixture (open-without-version, discovery, xtime, NaN) + synthetic cases (epoch decoding, arbitrary variable names, NaN-zeroing, missing-time rejection, rejects an eccad-layout file).
- `test_bc_pipeline` (integration) — runs the **full pipeline on the real subset** (`bc_anth_sum → BC`) to per-cell surface flux. This is the runnable MVP.
- Plus a `CreateUptempoTestNetCDF` synthetic-file helper and an `AcceptsUptempo` builder test.

## Docs
- User-guide "UPTEMPO on-mesh convention" section, a runnable README example, and an updated `test/data/README.md`.

## Plus (just now)
The reconciliation merge (`a87ee7d`) bringing #18 onto the clang-format-reformatted `main`.

**Scope notes:** the BC subset is black-carbon-only, so #6's NO2/NO/O3 stays on the synthetic path; ECCAD-native lat/lon + remapping remain out of scope. **Status:** `MERGEABLE`, **reviewer held** (your call), CI green except the Intel job I just re-ran (external repo 403 flake).

################################################################################
# Find Valgrind

if(MIEM_ENABLE_MEMCHECK)
  find_program(MEMORYCHECK_COMMAND "valgrind")
  set(MEMORYCHECK_COMMAND_OPTIONS "--error-exitcode=1" "--trace-children=yes" "--leak-check=full" "--gen-suppressions=all")
endif()

################################################################################
# Create a standard test that links to the MIEM library

function(create_standard_test)
  set(prefix TEST)
  set(singleValues NAME WORKING_DIRECTORY)
  set(multiValues SOURCES LIBRARIES)
  include(CMakeParseArguments)
  cmake_parse_arguments(${prefix} " " "${singleValues}" "${multiValues}" ${ARGN})

  add_executable(test_${TEST_NAME} ${TEST_SOURCES})
  target_link_libraries(test_${TEST_NAME} PUBLIC miem GTest::gtest_main)

  foreach(library ${TEST_LIBRARIES})
    target_link_libraries(test_${TEST_NAME} PUBLIC ${library})
  endforeach()

  if(NOT DEFINED TEST_WORKING_DIRECTORY)
    set(TEST_WORKING_DIRECTORY ${CMAKE_RUNTIME_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY})
  endif()

  add_test(NAME ${TEST_NAME}
          COMMAND test_${TEST_NAME}
          WORKING_DIRECTORY ${TEST_WORKING_DIRECTORY})

  if(MIEM_ENABLE_MEMCHECK AND MEMORYCHECK_COMMAND)
    add_test(NAME memcheck_${TEST_NAME}
            COMMAND ${MEMORYCHECK_COMMAND} ${MEMORYCHECK_COMMAND_OPTIONS} ${TEST_WORKING_DIRECTORY}/test_${TEST_NAME}
            WORKING_DIRECTORY ${TEST_WORKING_DIRECTORY})
  endif()

endfunction(create_standard_test)

################################################################################

function(create_standard_test)
  set(prefix TEST)
  set(singleValues NAME WORKING_DIRECTORY)
  set(multiValues SOURCES LIBRARIES)
  include(CMakeParseArguments)
  cmake_parse_arguments(${prefix} " " "${singleValues}" "${multiValues}" ${ARGN})
